title: Tuga A6 vs Tuga A8: Pocket Scanner or 8 Inch Rugged Tablet?
description: Tuga A6 handheld or Tuga A8 tablet, £50 apart. The A8 has the screen, battery and van dock; the A6 has a Zebra 2D scanner, a swappable battery and a pocket fit.
summary: £50 apart and both IP67: the A8 has the 8 inch 700 nit screen, 8GB of RAM, an 8500mAh battery, MIL-STD-810H and a dock connector; the A6 has a built-in Zebra 2D scan engine, a removable battery, dual SIM and fits a pocket at 277g.
lede: Buy the Tuga A8 at £399 if you fill in forms, read drawings or want a van mount; buy the Tuga A6 at £349 if you scan barcodes, want the device in a pocket or want to swap batteries. Both are rugged Android devices for sole traders and small firms, and £50 is too small a gap to decide on.
verdict: The A6 costs £349 and the A8 £399, a gap of £50, so price does not settle this one. They are different shapes of device for different work. Both are rugged Android devices sealed to IP67, with 4G, NFC and GPS, GLONASS, BeiDou and Galileo. The decision comes down to three things: whether you scan barcodes, whether you want to carry a tablet at all, and whether you want to swap batteries.

If you do not scan and do not need a pocket device, the A8 gives you more for £50. Its 8 inch screen against 6 helps with test schedules, long checklists and PDF drawings, and it is rated at 700 nits, where the A6 lists no brightness figure. It has 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage against 4GB and 64GB, on a MediaTek MT6789 against the A6's Helio P35, and an 8500mAh battery against 5050mAh. It is tested to MIL-STD-810H with a 1.22 metre drop rating, is rated to 60°C against the A6's 50°C, and has a full size USB-A port. Its 12 pin pogo connector fits the Charging Dock (£49.99) and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109), neither of which is listed for the A6. At 715g it suits a bag or a van door pocket rather than a trouser pocket.

Buy the A6 if you scan, work from a pocket or want a spare battery. It has a Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys, which the A8 does not have. Its 5050mAh battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over mid shift, where the A8's is built in. It has dual SIM where the A8 takes a single SIM, its maker rates it for 1.5 metre drops onto a wooden floor, and it runs Android 15 against the A8's Android 14, so check your apps on whichever you choose. Both include 12 months, and both can take the paid 3-Year Warranty at £65. See the electricians page and the field service page, or tell us what you fill in on site and we will say which we would buy.
chooseA: You scan parcels, stock or asset tags: the A6 has a Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys, and the A8 has no scanner.
You want one device that goes in a pocket or a Belt Holster (£22) rather than a tablet in a bag: the A6 weighs 277g against the A8's 715g, and the Belt Holster is not listed for the A8.
You want to swap batteries mid shift: the A6's 5050mAh battery is removable, and the A8's is built in.
You want two SIMs for patchy coverage: the A6 has dual SIM 4G, and the A8 takes a single SIM.
Your day is photos, job sheets, proof of delivery and sign-off, and a 6 inch screen at 2160 x 1080 is enough for that.
chooseB: You fill in forms, test schedules or long checklists on site and want 8 inches of screen rather than pinching and zooming on 6.
You work on bright roofs and open sites: the A8 is rated at 700 nits, and the A6 lists no brightness figure.
You want MIL-STD-810H: the A8 is tested to it with a 1.22 metre drop rating, where the A6 has its maker's 1.5 metre rating onto a wooden floor and no MIL-STD rating.
You want it on the dashboard or in a desk dock: the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) and the Charging Dock (£49.99) fit the A8's pogo connector and are not listed for the A6.
You run heavier apps or keep a lot on the device: 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage against 4GB and 64GB, and an 8500mAh battery against 5050mAh.

faq.q: Is the Tuga A8 worth £50 more than the A6?
faq.a: If you do not scan and do not need to swap batteries, yes. For £50 more the A8 has the 8 inch 700 nit Full HD screen, a larger 8500mAh battery, twice the RAM and storage, MIL-STD-810H, a USB-A port and a dock connector for the vehicle dock, so for forms, test schedules, checklists, drawings and PDFs it is the better buy. If your work is scanning parcels, stock or asset tags, you want the device in a pocket, or you want a charged spare battery, the A6 at £349 is the one: it has the Zebra 2D scan engine the A8 lacks, a removable battery, dual SIM and Android 15 against Android 14, and it weighs 277g.

faq.q: Can I do forms on the A6 instead of buying a tablet?
faq.a: Short ones should be fine, but check your own app first. The A6 screen is 6 inches at 2160 x 1080, a pocket-sized screen suited to short job sheets, scans and signatures. Long forms and drawings mean a lot of scrolling, pinching and zooming, which is where the A8 starts to pay for itself. The A6 has 4GB of RAM on a Helio P35 against the A8's 8GB on a MediaTek MT6789, so try your heaviest app. Open the longest form you fill in on a typical day and see whether you can work through it one-handed. The Capacitive Stylus (£14.99) is listed for the A8 but not for the A6, which matters if you want a stylus for customer signatures.

faq.q: Which is tougher, the A6 or the A8?
faq.a: Both are sealed to IP67, which covers dust and short immersion, so both are sealed against rain and a drop in a puddle. Beyond that, the A8 has more listed: it is tested to MIL-STD-810H with a 1.22 metre drop rating and rated to work from -20°C to 60°C. The A6 has its maker's own rating for 1.5 metre drops onto a wooden floor, with no MIL-STD rating, and works from -20°C to 50°C. The two drop figures come from different tests, so do not read the higher number as the tougher device. Our IP rating guide and MIL-STD-810H guide explain what each rating does and does not test.

faq.q: Can I mount the A6 in the van like the A8?
faq.a: Not with the same dock. The A8 has a 12 pin pogo connector, and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109), a locking VESA mount with DC power input, is listed for the A8, A10, W8 and W10. It is not listed for the A6. What fits the A6 is the Car Phone Mount (£17), a heavy duty suction cup mount for rugged handhelds, and the 12V DC Car Charger (£26) fits both. The A6 has charging contacts on the body, but no dock or cradle is listed for it. So the A6 can sit in a suction cup mount and charge from the 12V socket, but if you want a locked-in dashboard unit that comes out as the site tablet, that is the A8. Everything is on the accessories page.
